name: AppShell
summary: Application frame: sidebar, topbar and main content.

props.name: brand
props.description: Logotype and product name. Lives in the topbar, beside the navigation toggle.

props.name: navigation
props.description: The sidebar content, usually a <nav>. The shell never invents one, so the landmark and its label are yours.

props.name: navItems
props.description: The sidebar list, handed to the Sidebar the shell already creates — same shape as Sidebar items. Use this instead of passing a second <Sidebar> as navigation: that nests two panels, two borders and two 22px radii, and the inner one clips its text. When navigation is also given, the list comes first.

props.name: currentNavId
props.description: The id of the current item in navItems. Marked with aria-current="page" and the selected skin.

props.name: navLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the <nav> built from navItems. Falls back to the sidebarLabel string.

props.name: topbar
props.description: What sits in the topbar next to the brand: sections, search, actions.

props.name: topbarVariant
props.description: Skin of the topbar. flush removes the outer gap, and the sidebar rises to meet it.

props.name: sidebarVariant
props.description: Skin of the sidebar, forwarded to it. flush is the one exception this design system makes to its floating surfaces: the panel sits against the edges, takes the full height and is separated from the content by a single rule. Without this prop the variant would be unreachable for anyone composing through the shell, which is the normal path.

props.name: sidebarScrollbar
props.description: The left sidebar's scrollbar, forwarded to it: hover (light, shown with the pointer over it, with focus inside and on touch screens) or visible (always on screen).

props.name: sidebarCollapsed
props.description: Narrows the sidebar panel to --sidebar-rail. A floating panel keeps its two outer margins in the grid track; flush uses the token as the raw track width. Controlled by you, like the palette's open: the shell does not decide when to collapse. Without sidebarCollapsible it draws no button; with it, the button calls onSidebarCollapsedChange and you decide. Below 1024px the drawer is never a rail, controlled or not: collapsed inside the drawer it was a column of unnamed icons.

props.name: sidebarCollapsible
props.description: Draws the collapse button at the top of the junction between the sidebar and the content — centred on the gap, level with the first item, sticky with the sidebar — and turns the sidebar into the rail on its own between 1024 and 1279px. Off by default: without it the shell is exactly the one before, and an app that already drives sidebarCollapsed with its own button does not get a second one. Behaviour read from the sidebar that one of the references uses (the main reference library has no app frame).

props.name: defaultSidebarCollapsed
props.description: Starts collapsed without controlling it. The person's choice holds until the window crosses 1280px; then the width decides again.

props.name: onSidebarCollapsedChange
props.description: Called on every change — the button, or the width crossing 1280px. Keeping the preference is the app's job, as before.

props.name: children
props.description: Page content. Rendered inside the <main> the shell owns.

props.name: topbarDivider
props.description: Passes Topbar's `divider` to the flush bar the shell builds.

props.name: layout
props.description: The arrangement. docs is the one of the reference documentation: one block of 1400 in the middle of the screen with the sidebar (220), the text and, from 1280 up, the table of contents (240 at the start of a 268 column); the bar on top is the small one, on the same block. Both columns start 16 below the bar and stop 32 above the bottom of the screen; inside the sidebar, 16 on both sides and 8 inside each item; the table of contents shows no scrollbar. Below 1024 the sidebar is the drawer and the text keeps 24 from the edge.

props.name: topbarTabs
props.description: The second row of the bar on top: the site's areas, forwarded as the Header's tabs.

props.name: topbarCurrentTab
props.description: The id of the current area, forwarded as the Header's currentTab.

props.name: topbarTabsLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the second row, forwarded as the Header's tabsLabel.

props.name: contentVariant
props.description: `plain` removes the box around the content area. `.content` is a card — same background, border and radius as `.card` — so a Card inside it would be a box inside an identical box. The margin stays.

props.name: aside
props.description: The right-hand column — a documentation page's "On this page" (a TableOfContents). From 1280 up it is the third column; below, it follows the content.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: The right column's name for screen readers.

props.name: asideVariant
props.description: Skin of the right-hand column. Without it, the same as the left sidebar. plain removes the box — the items sit loose on the page, like a documentation page's "On this page".

a11y.notes: Below the lg breakpoint (1024px) the sidebar becomes a drawer: a native popover invoked by the topbar toggle. Escape, click-outside and aria-expanded on the toggle are native; AppShell normalises entry and focus return across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Non-modal by design — focus is not trapped, so no modality is declared that is not delivered.
a11y.nota: Escape closes the navigation drawer; Tab moves into the drawer right after the toggle. This sentence used to live inside a11y.keyboard, where it counted as two declared keys and no reader of the contract could find it.
